sections.title: Profile
sections.text: Zima, leader of the Ursus Student Self-Governing Group. Since joining Rhodes Island she has long served as a squad captain, and more recently made significant contributions by helping Rhodes Island establish its office in Deity Grypherburg. Through prolonged training and frequent combat, Zima has honed her abilities and formed a distinctive, mature fighting style. She now takes part in Rhodes Island's operations in Ursus as a Guard Operator.

sections.title: Archive File 1
sections.text:
In the summer of 1101, when Sonya Mikhailovna signed her name at the bottom of the disembarkation checklist alongside the other members of the Ursus Student Self-Governing Group, she never imagined that the journey ahead would prove far more winding than she had anticipated.
The road to Ursus was nowhere near as clear or as constant as the temperature inside the transport's passenger cabin. The first stop on the itinerary arrived soon enough, and the Ursus Student Self-Governing Group did indeed set foot on snow-covered ground—except that the ground was Kjerag's.
By Zima's recollection, the moment Leto had dumped a great heap of name-tagged luggage at the station, she dragged everyone off to the snowy mountain sights, whooping and hollering the whole way and startling more than a few shared burdenbeasts that had been enjoying the sun. Instructor Dur-nar warned them countless times to keep away from the cliff edges, to no effect whatsoever, and in the end she had to tie everyone's safety lines to herself all at once. What left the deepest impression on Zima, however, was the scene as they departed: when a station attendant brought over the bill for their overdue luggage storage, Leto breezily signed that staggering sum with the surname 'Paleroche,' adding, 'Gifts. Hand them out for me.' Once the train pulled away, Leto pointed at the tall figure standing on the platform with a very complicated look on their face and laughed until she could hardly stand up straight. Only after laughing for quite a while did she tell Zima that the pile of 'gifts' they had just abandoned seemed to hold not only the 'junk' she had meant to throw out from the start, but also the cold-weather clothing and every last snack they would need for the rest of the trip.
Consequently, the first thing the Ursus Student Self-Governing Group did upon reaching Deity Grypherburg was not to submit their university applications, but to buy more clothes. Even after enrolling successfully at a university within Deity Grypherburg, Zima did not forget the task Rhodes Island had entrusted to her. The social mood of Deity Grypherburg was just beginning to show a kind of premonitory anxiety and excitement: upheavals in other nations had become powerful ammunition for every sort of theory, and everyone wanted their own voice heard, to point out the way forward for Ursus. To Zima, the climate of opinion inside Deity Grypherburg was far too tangled, and far too remote from the problems of real life. And so, accompanied by Instructor Dur-nar, Zima began using her holidays to travel out to the nomadic cities and settlements nearby, observing how the people there lived, recording the problems they faced, collecting their arguments, and trying to work out how much of it had been imported and how much had grown from that soil.
Zima's fieldwork, however, was forced to end early. What happened in the Far North changed everything. The Empire's public discourse tightened at once, the warships of the armies were constantly on the move, and snow began to fall across the whole of Ursus... Zima returned alone to Deity Grypherburg, carrying everything she had thought and understood in that time. What she did not expect was that what awaited her was more than just a 'Student Joint Assembly.'

sections.title: Archive File 2
sections.text:
After the 'Katorga Incident' came to an end, the tension hanging in the air of Deity Grypherburg was not relieved in the slightest—if anything, it showed every sign of intensifying.
For the citizens of Deity Grypherburg, some of the changes were plain to the naked eye: the hours of power supply had not been extended, and its frequency had grown even less stable; the Katorga District remained firmly locked onto Deity Grypherburg's engine layer, yet a few of its chimneys had begun to vent white steam; the toppled statue of Emperor Igor simply lay where it was, and like the broken city wall, no one repaired it, no one defaced it, and no one even dared spare it a second glance in passing.
Other changes, however, were known to almost no one: the 'Ursus Student Self-Governing Group,' with Zima at its head, was never found guilty of anything, the whole matter apparently having been quietly buried through some deliberate maneuvering. Nor were they able, in the end, to travel with Crownslayer to the region where Gummy's parents were—Amiya contacted Zima and Gummy personally to explain the reasons, while the Doctor signed the personnel paperwork in person, appointing Zima as the coordinator in charge of establishing Rhodes Island's office in Deity Grypherburg.

[Audio Log]
'I understand the position Rhodes Island is in. In Ursus, Rhodes Island sticks out like a drop of blood in the snow. We can't go swaggering about stringing up comm lines, or shipping a whole crowd of people into Deity Grypherburg. That is exactly why our work matters so much. Setting up the Deity Grypherburg office takes more than premises—yes, thank you for scrubbing out these rehearsal rooms, Gummy—we also need funds, we need connections, we need to make sure those nobles aren't coming around to hassle us every other day, we need a business that visibly operates aboveboard, we need people dedicated to reception and liaison, and every bit of it we have to sort out ourselves. Sounds hard, doesn't it? Luckily we have some experience with this sort of thing, and we each have something we're good at... What? You want to work the front desk? No. Not you, Ukusik. Anyone else, but not you, or we'll be out of business inside a week—hey, hold on, who said you could sit in on this? This is a closed meeting! Trying to sneak off? Too late! Now that you've heard our secrets, you had better hurry up and sign this employment application. Istina, this doesn't count as breaking the rules, does it? Good.'

I'm up to my neck in work right now, so I'm just going to dash this report brief off. I don't have that kind of time.
You would not believe how much trouble it is to register and run a pharmaceutical company's office in Deity Grypherburg! Take today: I received a notice saying our scheduled fire inspection had been pushed back, because we were in violation of one of the safety standards. We spent an entire day digging into it, and guess what the reason turned out to be?
It was my big, heavy hammer-axe. Too 'frightening,' and therefore unsafe—what kind of logic is that?
And you'll never guess how we ended up solving it. We found a glass case, put it over the hammer-axe, and declared it a cultural relic on display.
And that... was that.
Honestly, if I had known ahead of time that all this would be such a hassle, I'd have been better off running off to ■■■■ and swinging my hammer-axe through a few good fights!
—Operator Zima's 'Report Brief'

sections.title: Archive File 3
sections.text:
Zima and Istina once had a conversation.
Afterwards, each of them voluntarily reported the conversation to Rhodes Island's Medical Department, to be filed as records for their mental health care procedures.

I've never been someone who's good with words. Even at the moment I opened my mouth, I hadn't worked out what I was actually going to say.
So Istina and I started with the Katorga District. I told her what I had run into inside, and she told me what she had been through outside.
I told her what happened to Leonid, how strongly Fadey objected at first to us going to rescue our own classmate, how furious I was in that moment, how badly I wanted to knock that guy flat on the ground and then go do what needed doing. But I didn't do it. In that instant, I started wondering: if it were Istina standing there, what would she do? I don't know. Maybe by then Istina would already have listed four or five reasons and shut those objecting idiots right up. But she wasn't there.
I held back the urge to throw a punch, or to slap him. I forced myself to calm down and solve the problem the way Istina would. I can't come out with lines that sharp and elegant, so I just spoke slowly, and laid out the principles I firmly believe in. As long as I am convinced those principles are right, they ought to be able to convince other people too. Yes, that's what I did, and looking back on it, I think I got it right.
Right? That's what I asked Istina. I also told her that, honestly, I regret not slapping Fadey back then.
But she said: Sonya, I'm glad. Not because of what you did, but because you regret it now—inside, you are still holding on to yourself.
I don't get what she meant by that. It sounded a bit like sarcasm, and yet somehow I found myself agreeing with it. Huh, strange—thinking back now on talking all this over with Istina, it actually moves me a little.
—Operator Zima's interview record

'Moved'? Not in the least. If Sonya hadn't been so greedy, dragging me off to steal Instructor Dur-nar's cupcakes before they had even finished baking, I would never have been clumsily locked inside the kitchen prep room by her. Waiting for Instructor Dur-nar to hear the alarm and open the door to rescue the two of us thieves is the most embarrassing thing I have been through in recent memory.
As for the things she said... they are quite true, but they were not sarcasm. In fact, while I was doing what I did outside the Katorga District, I often forced myself into Sonya's role, and asked myself: if it were Sonya, what would she do? In the same way, I have my regrets too. Regret does not mean that you did anything wrong; it is simply confirmation that you are still holding on to yourself.
Of course, Sonya could perfectly well have delivered that slap, and I could perfectly well have refrained from pushing myself that far. The outcome? Who could say whether the things that never happened would have been good or bad? At the very least, we are both asking ourselves the question now, and that is enough.
Oh, one more thing. When Instructor Dur-nar arrived, Sonya slipped away at once, and there was one thing I never got to say to her properly. As you know, once you are out of that particular setting, some things become much harder to say. So I may as well say it here—
Sonya, I am glad that in this moment, both of us held on to ourselves. I think that is exactly why we will always be able to trust each other.
—Operator Istina's interview record

By the time I got in there, the two of them had all but polished off that batch of cupcakes. Hehe... it's fine. That's exactly why I love baking.
—Operator Dur-nar

sections.title: Archive File 4
sections.text:
We have beaten those bastards. We are free at last. What comes next is to gather more hands, to call upon everyone willing to join us! We will take the whole of Deity Grypherburg, and prove who the true masters of this place are!
—Words on a sheet of paper

I have seen the people groaning in pain, I have seen the land covered in scars. This soil can no longer be squeezed for a single drop of milk, and yet those greedy nobles and hateful bureaucrats still torment it like leeches—torment our homeland. I must resist. I will take up the blade! And I know I am far from the only one who thinks this way.
—Words on a sheet of paper

We cut off the police chief's head. We will cut off many more heads yet! This rotten country will not hold out much longer! We will win! Nika, Sonya... I fight for you.
—Words on a sheet of paper

While cleaning out the abandoned theater that served as the Ursus Student Self-Governing Group's temporary base of activity, Zima and Gummy happened to find a great stack of documents in the basement, along with many sheets of paper covered in writing.
At first she took them for some sort of script, full of nonsensical lines. But after Absinthe looked through some municipal planning records, she discovered that this basement had existed before the theater was ever built: long ago, a very long time ago, two or three centuries back, this place had already been part of a prison, used mainly to store and destroy the belongings stripped from condemned prisoners.
So Zima began to look at those sheets again. Condemned prisoners capable of writing such things had most likely committed the great crime of treason and rebellion, and had in the end been put down and arrested by Ursus's military police. Looking closely, the texture and color of every sheet differed, and the handwriting on them came from different hands.
That meant that over the course of several centuries there had been many uprisings, large and small—some to resist crushing taxes, some to take revenge on corrupt officials and cruel magistrates. Those who left these words behind were farmers, or poets, or soldiers, or madmen... The eras they lived in were far apart: some wrote in factories driven by Originium external combustion engines, while others had only just heard of the newly invented 'Originium external combustion engine.' In the end, though, their final words were all piled up in the same dark corner.
Zima tried to establish the identities of those who had left the writings behind, but unsurprisingly, neither those tumultuous 'rebellions' nor the people who raised the banner of resistance had left so much as a name in the vast history of Ursus.

What I'm thinking about is a little childish, I suppose. I'm thinking about how many Sonyas Ursus has had over these last few centuries. How many Annas, Rosalinds, Ladas, Natalyas, Zoyas... and how many Pyotrs and Ivans?
When I saw the name 'Sonya' written on that sheet, I couldn't help but shiver. Why was it me who found these things—fate, or coincidence?
I set down the paper in my hand and looked around that basement packed with dust-covered history, and what I thought was: this time, it should be different.
I will make the outcome different.
—Operator Zima

sections.title: Promotion Record
sections.text:
[Classified Log]
According to the after-action reports later submitted by Operator Zima and the others, they in fact ran into no small number of unexpected incidents over the course of planning the entire 'Rescue Student Laleya' operation—a figure flickering past the window during a secret meeting, a schedule vanishing inexplicably from a locked storeroom... On the day of the operation itself, some of the students responsible for transporting logistical supplies were even stopped in an alley and closely questioned by policemen who had removed their epaulettes. It seems their plan was enough to fool the nobles at the hearing, but not enough to escape certain eyes watching from on high.
What Operator Zima emphasized most in her after-action report, however, was this: every one of those incidents ultimately came to nothing, and even the stamped and sealed warrants for their arrest were quietly rescinded. By her own account, Zima assumed at the time that this was the result of Rhodes Island's mediation behind the scenes, and found it rather surprising that Rhodes Island could clear up such troubles for them so easily, and yet struggle to get a long-range communication device delivered.
In truth, ever since the Far North Incident, every activity Rhodes Island undertakes within Ursus's borders has met with immense resistance, as though a pair of invisible eyes at the very top of Deity Grypherburg were watching our every move at all times.
We have no way of determining the intentions of those in power in Ursus, nor is now the best moment to attempt direct communication. Especially after the ■■■■ Incident, we must re-examine this ancient nation of Ursus and the vast, intricate system by which it runs.
